MEDIA STATEMENT
03 March 2025
THE REGULATOR WELCOMES THE JUSTICE MINISTER’S DECISION ON PUBLICATION OF THE
SEX OFFENDERS REGISTER
The Information Regulator (Regulator) welcomes the decision by the Minister of Justice & Constitutional
Development, the Hon. Mmamoloko Kubayi MP (the Minister), to put a pause on the publication of the
National Register of Sex Offenders (NRSO). According to the statement released on 01 March 2025 by
the Department of Justice & Constitutional Development (DoJ&CD), this decision was arrived at after
consideration of “the confidentiality and disclosure provisions in the Sexual Offences and Related
Matters Act”. The Regulator supports the Minister’s decision fully. Sexual assault and gender-based
violence are doubtlessly a scourge in South Africa and all legally sound actions must be taken to protect
the vulnerable against such egregious violations of their rights to bodily integrity and human dignity.
However, in a rules-based society such as South Africa, it is also imperative that such action must fall
within the confines of the law.
Currently, the legislation providing for the compilation, maintenance and dissemination of the NRSO
prohibits its publication. This was one of the issues discussed by the Regulator and the representatives
of the DoJ&CD at their meeting held on 27 January 2028. An additional concern for the Regulator was
that it was not clear how the DoJ&CD intended to ensure that the publication of the NRSO would be
consistent with the eight conditions for lawful processing of personal information in terms of the
Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA).
